questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most crucial ascpect choosing my study destination was the availabilty of having different courses that fit my study track (Policy, Financing and Health Care Systems). Furthermore, a lot of courses were not available for exchange students e.g. in Sydney which made the selection very limited for me. However, due to the fact that my first choice for Washington D.C. was cancelled the choices in the  second round were generally very limited for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a fantastic time in Australia, and I don't want to pass up this opportunity. The courses I could select at the University of Melbourne, however, were quite similar to those I had taken in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to get information. I received emails in terms of welcome day/week and everything i needed to know for arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I could go to the information center whenever I had any questions. It was open to all students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They were really helpful in the information center which was called Stop 1.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find housing. There are a lot of students accomodations available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Most of the accommondations are very close to the campus so it is very easy to get around. 
However, I would recommend future exchange students to inform themselves about options that are not directly offered by the university because sometimes there are cheaper options. Also, the prices per week vary extremely. Therefore, I would recommend to get several offers from different dormitories.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My dorm (unilodge lincoln house) was extremely expensive for what they offered. The rooms very extremely small and the shared bathroom were never really cleaned. For me personally it was the worst and dirtiest dorm i have ever lived in. Especially considering the extremely high price. Therefore i really can't recommend this dorm to other students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First i had to send a pre-approval plan with max 10 courses to the university in melbourne. once these were approved i could register for 4 courses via a website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an information center where i could write a email when i had questions regarding the registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The choice of courses in the winter semester was limited for me personally. I wanted to enroll in health management courses, but they were only available in the summer semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The registration process was very easy therefore i don't have an advices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general, the courses were very repetitive for me since I had most of the content already in Copenhagen. The content of the courses was very basic and therefore i had the feeling to learn little new content.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very different compared to the University of Copenhagen. Every class required seeing a video in general. The content of the lecture was delivered in this video. The purpose of the in-person presentation was then to discuss the information in the video. Additionally, there were a number of group presentations that occupied a lot of the lecture.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Women and Global Health
Social Determinants of Health Inequality
Primary Health Care and Global Health
Comparative Health Systems

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depending on the Master programme but courses i took were very repetative.

How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a very high number of sports/social activities offered by the university. There was even a swimming pool on campus that I went to once a week. I also went running a lot because there was an athletic group at the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can't make any recommendations because it depends on the personal interests of the person. However, there are more than 200 societies and clubs so everyone can find something!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Melbourne. Especially Phillip Island and Mornington Peninsula. Renting a car is very easy you just need an international driver license.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy since Australia is very similar to Europe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend living in a student dorm. There it is very easy to get in contact with other international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: What i noticed most is that australians are very friendly and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Compare prices for the student dorms. 
Plan enough time to travel afterwards. 
Australia is more expensive than you think ;)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The best part of my exchange was that I met 4 friends for life who made my time unforgettable

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge for myself was the weather. I arrived in Melbourne in July and therefore didn't have a long summer in Europe. It was mostly cold, windy and rainy in Melbourne.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
